title: Appraisal Order Late-Rush Refund Counting Rule
content:
### Counting rule of the Appraisal Order late-rush refund

**Clause.** The counting rule of the late-rush refund picks the date the days late run to: when the order carries reconsideration decisions that changed the value, they run to the decided date of the latest such decision; when the copy reached the borrower more than 2 calendar days after the completed date, they run to the date the copy was delivered to the borrower; otherwise they run to the completed date. The days late run from the due date of the Appraisal Order, in calendar days. The days late of the late-rush refund are this refund's own count; the appraisal delay, the calendar days from the due date to the completed date that other Larkspur rules rely on, is unchanged.

**Order of the tests.** The tests are read in the order written: a value-changing reconsideration decision on the order settles the date whatever the delivery date; the delivery test applies only to an order with no such decision.

| Reconsideration decision on the order that changed the value | Copy delivered to the borrower, after the completed date | Days late run to |
|---|---|---|
| Yes (one or more) | Any | Decided date of the latest value-changing decision |
| No | More than 2 calendar days after | Date the copy was delivered to the borrower |
| No | 2 calendar days after or sooner, or not yet delivered | Completed date |

A reconsideration decision that left the value unchanged, or a request returned incomplete, is not a decision that changed the value.

**Hypothetical dates (due date the 10th, completed the 12th).**
- Copy delivered on the 14th (2 days after completion), no value-changing decision: days late run to the 12th, giving 2.
- Copy delivered on the 15th (3 days after completion), no value-changing decision: they run to the 15th, giving 5.
- Value-changing decision dated the 28th, copy delivered on the 15th: they run to the 28th, giving 18.
